content:
Río Bravo, Tamaulipas Mayor Miguel Ángel Almaraz Maldonado was found alive on Sunday after armed men seized him and his family on a highway in Zacatecas the night before, federal Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch announced.

Almaraz, who took office on October 1, 2024, after winning election as a National Action Party candidate, was reported missing on Saturday evening, November 7, while traveling with family members toward the town of Real de Catorce in San Luis Potosí, according to RÉCORD and other Mexican outlets. Armed men intercepted the vehicles they were traveling in on the San Tiburcio–Vanegas highway in Zacatecas. Some of his companions were freed and reached the town of Cedral, San Luis Potosí, to ask for help, and his wife reported the incident to investigators in Río Bravo.

Harfuch announced on Sunday that the mayor had been located by the federal Gabinete de Seguridad, working with authorities from Zacatecas, Coahuila, San Luis Potosí and Tamaulipas, and he posted a photo of the mayor with security personnel. Authorities have not yet said exactly where he was found, how he was freed, or whether anyone was detained.

State authorities gave conflicting accounts of where the seizure happened: San Luis Potosí officials said it took place on the San Tiburcio–Vanegas highway in Zacatecas, while Tamaulipas officials initially said it happened in San Luis Potosí.

The search involved federal forces and authorities from four states. Río Bravo, Tamaulipas, is the border city near McAllen, Texas — not Rio Bravo, Texas, in Webb County.

Update — November 8, 2026 (Sunday evening)

New details emerged Sunday evening about how the mayor regained his freedom. According to authorities in San Luis Potosí, Almaraz was taken to the city of Zacatecas and released there, then traveled north on his own by public transport until Coahuila state police found him at a security checkpoint on Federal Highway 54 near Saltillo, on the Coahuila–Zacatecas border. Coahuila police took him into their care, gave him a medical check, food and water, and placed him under the protection of the state prosecutor’s office, according to the accounts.

Harfuch described the recovery as the result of a coordinated federal operation. The Coahuila account indicates the mayor had already been released before state police found him at the checkpoint — no rescue from captivity was reported.

The conflicting accounts of where the seizure happened grew to three on Sunday: Zacatecas state prosecutor Cristian Paul Camacho said the events took place in Cedral, San Luis Potosí, contradicting the San Luis Potosí security secretariat’s statement that the seizure happened on the San Tiburcio–Vanegas highway in Zacatecas.

As of Sunday evening, authorities had announced no arrests and had not said who seized the mayor or why. The mayor was giving his statement to investigators, according to the reports.

Update — November 9, 2026 (Monday)

Mayor Almaraz told reporters on Monday that he escaped from his captors, giving a different account from the official version reported Sunday evening. He said he was held in a pasture with another man, and when his captors left the area he jumped a fence and ran for about an hour, then walked through the night — about 80 kilometers in all — before boarding a passenger bus and reaching a Coahuila state police checkpoint on the Coahuila–Zacatecas border, where he identified himself and asked for help. He said he suffered no blows or injuries but was badly frightened.

His account differs from the version reported Sunday evening, in which San Luis Potosí authorities said he had been taken to the city of Zacatecas and released there. The mayor has returned home to Río Bravo, and the Tamaulipas state prosecutor's office confirmed his safe transfer back and said the investigation continues.

The Tamaulipas prosecutor's office said Monday the mayor had not yet given a formal declaration to investigators, so his account to reporters is his own testimony, not yet a formal ministerial statement. As of Monday, authorities had still not publicly identified who seized him or why, and no arrests had been announced.

Sources: Expresión Sonora / El Chamuco, November 9, 2026; Lado.mx, November 9, 2026; Radar Nacional MX, November 9, 2026.

Sources: RÉCORD, November 8, 2026; Emeequis, November 8, 2026; El Horizonte, November 8, 2026.

Sources: BINoticias, November 8, 2026; Análisis, November 8, 2026; El Diario El Valle, November 8, 2026.

title: Río Bravo mayor found alive after armed men seized him on a Zacatecas highway
